slides.title: 01 / INTRODUCTION
slides.raw_text: 01 / INTRODUCTION Introduction & project background Video creation has become a regular requirement for education, marketing, social media and digital communication. VIDAI EDITOR  |  PROJECT PRESENTATION 02 BACKGROUND Growing content demand Creators frequently work with long recordings and need shorter, clear and engaging outputs for multiple platforms. Fragmented workflow Editing, audio cleanup, highlight selection and cover design are often handled in separate tools. Time and complexity Repeated imports, exports and manual coordination increase production time and make project organisation harder. Need A unified workflow can reduce tool switching and keep decisions connected to one project. PROJECT INTRODUCTION VidAI Editor A central video workspace designed to manage the journey from source media to final deliverables. Integrated processing The system brings together editing, media analysis, audio improvement and visual packaging. Creator control Automated suggestions support the user; final edits and publishing decisions remain editable. Intended users Content creators, students, educators, small teams and social-media producers.

slides.title: 02 / PROJECT DEFINITION
slides.raw_text: 02 / PROJECT DEFINITION Problem statement, objectives & scope The project focuses on making the overall production process more connected, manageable and repeatable. VIDAI EDITOR  |  PROJECT PRESENTATION 03 PROBLEM STATEMENT Scattered tools Media tasks are spread across different applications and workflows. Manual effort Finding useful moments and preparing media can take significant time. Inconsistent output Different export settings and disconnected assets can lead to avoidable rework. OBJECTIVES Unified workspace Manage source files, edits and outputs under one project. Faster workflow Assist users with media analysis and repeatable processing. Reliable delivery Make output settings, processing status and project versions clear. PROJECT SCOPE Included Project organisation, editing workflow, media analysis, audio processing, visual packaging and export planning. User role Review suggestions, adjust settings and approve final results. Boundary Advanced semantic understanding and guaranteed engagement prediction are not assumed.

slides.title: 03 / PROPOSED SOLUTION
slides.raw_text: 03 / PROPOSED SOLUTION Proposed system & working methodology A project-centred workflow connects each stage through shared media assets and saved editing decisions. VIDAI EDITOR  |  PROJECT PRESENTATION 04 END-TO-END METHOD 1. Project setup Create a project and define its target format, media requirements and output preferences. 2. Media intake Upload source video/audio, validate files and register asset metadata. 3. Analyse and prepare Inspect media signals, identify candidate moments and prepare audio or visual assets. 4. Edit and review Arrange segments, refine timing, preview changes and approve the sequence. 5. Render and deliver Process the approved edit, verify the generated file and store project outputs. METHODOLOGY PRINCIPLES Single source of truth The project record links original media, edit decisions, processing settings and generated files. Non-destructive editing Keep originals intact; save edits as instructions and create new output versions. Human-in-the-loop Automated analysis proposes candidates; the creator decides what belongs in the final result. Repeatability Save settings and versions so a project can be reviewed or rendered again. Status visibility Show queued, processing, completed and failed states with useful messages.

slides.title: 04 / TECHNOLOGY STACK
slides.raw_text: 04 / TECHNOLOGY STACK Technology used The platform uses web technologies for the interactive workspace and media-processing tools for analysis and output. VIDAI EDITOR  |  PROJECT PRESENTATION 05 FRONTEND & USER EXPERIENCE React 19 Component-based interface for the project workspace. TypeScript Typed application logic and maintainable data structures. Vite Development server and frontend build tooling. Tailwind CSS Utility-based styling and responsive layouts. Framer Motion / Lucide Interface transitions and iconography. DATA & APPLICATION SERVICES Supabase PostgreSQL-backed data access and project metadata. Supabase JS Frontend integration with backend services. API routes Project, video and edit operations through HTTP endpoints. Storage layer Media files and generated outputs require managed object storage. Queue service A background queue is recommended for long-running processing. MEDIA & PROCESSING Web Audio API Decode and analyse audio in the browser. FFT / spectral DSP Frequency-domain noise estimation and suppression. Canvas & video APIs Frame extraction, image composition and preview. FFmpeg Recommended rendering engine for real trimming, concatenation and encoding. Python / OpenCV Recommended extension for advanced media analysis.

Background workers Handle longer media tasks without blocking normal web requests.

slides.title: 06 / SYSTEM DESIGN
slides.raw_text: 06 / SYSTEM DESIGN System architecture & data management A layered design keeps the interface responsive while media jobs run independently. VIDAI EDITOR  |  PROJECT PRESENTATION 07 PRESENTATION LAYER Web client React + TypeScript application. Workspace Project dashboard, media library, preview and editing controls. Client tasks Frame capture, audio preview and lightweight analysis. APPLICATION LAYER API Authentication, project access, asset registration and job creation. Database Users, projects, assets, edit versions and processing records. Storage Private source media, intermediate files and final deliverables. Queue Dispatch long-running work to processing workers. PROCESSING LAYER Analysis worker Audio/visual measurements and candidate generation. Enhancement worker Audio filtering and noise reduction. Render worker FFmpeg-based assembly, filtering and encoding. Delivery Store output, update job state and provide secure access.

slides.title: 07 / TECHNICAL APPROACH
slides.raw_text: 07 / TECHNICAL APPROACH Algorithms & processing concepts The platform combines signal processing, media measurements and deterministic rendering. VIDAI EDITOR  |  PROJECT PRESENTATION 08 MEDIA ANALYSIS Audio energy Short-window RMS and peak amplitude estimate changes in audio intensity. Visual activity Frame-to-frame pixel differences estimate movement between sampled frames. Candidate ranking Normalised audio and visual signals are combined to prioritise intervals for review. Overlap filtering Sliding windows and overlap suppression reduce duplicate suggestions. AUDIO PROCESSING Low-frequency filtering Optional low-cut filtering reduces rumble. Short-time Fourier transform Windowed audio frames are transformed into frequency components. Noise profile Quiet frames estimate the background-noise spectrum. Spectral gating Frequency bins are attenuated according to the estimated noise profile. Normalisation Output peak level is adjusted for more consistent playback. EDIT & RENDER LOGIC Edit decision list Store ordered source ranges, in/out points and track settings. Timeline mapping Map each selected source interval to its output position. Filter graph Apply crop, scale, audio gain and other requested transformations. Encoding Render an MP4 with compatible video/audio codecs and verify playback. Analysis scores are assistance signals—not proof of meaning, emotion or likely audience engagement.

slides.title: 08 / EVALUATION
slides.raw_text: 08 / EVALUATION Expected benefits, testing & current limitations A useful product is measured by output quality, workflow reliability and the time required to complete a project. VIDAI EDITOR  |  PROJECT PRESENTATION 09 EXPECTED BENEFITS Centralised workflow One project keeps media and production decisions organised. Reduced repetition Reusable settings and saved edits reduce repeated manual setup. Creator flexibility Suggestions can be reviewed and changed before export. Consistent delivery Shared output settings help standardise project results. TESTING APPROACH Functional tests Upload, project creation, edit saving and output retrieval. Media tests Different resolutions, codecs, aspect ratios and audio conditions. Quality checks A/V sync, cut accuracy, audio clarity and thumbnail readability. Reliability tests Large files, failed jobs, retries and interrupted uploads. LIMITATIONS TO ADDRESS Render completeness A production export pipeline must generate a real encoded video. Analysis accuracy Motion and energy heuristics can miss context or rank irrelevant moments. Audio trade-offs Strong denoising may affect quiet speech or natural sound. Scalability Large media files require storage, queues and worker resource limits.

slides.title: 09 / CLOSING
slides.raw_text: 09 / CLOSING Future scope & conclusion The long-term direction is a dependable creator platform with progressively smarter assistance. VIDAI EDITOR  |  PROJECT PRESENTATION 10 FUTURE SCOPE Speech intelligence Add voice activity detection, transcription and searchable timestamps. Scene understanding Add shot-boundary detection, scene grouping and object-aware search. Smarter highlights Train ranking models using creator selections and feedback. Advanced editing Add subtitles, transitions, presets, multi-track editing and batch exports. Collaboration Add shared projects, comments, roles and review approvals. CONCLUSION Project summary VidAI Editor is designed as one connected workflow for preparing, editing and delivering video content. Core value It brings media organisation, assisted analysis, audio processing, visual packaging and export into a common project structure. Engineering priority The most important next step is a reliable end-to-end render pipeline with secure storage and background processing. Final outcome A practical foundation that can evolve from a unified editing workspace into an intelligent video production platform.
